newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resids mostly hold, HSFO slips.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resids mostly hold, HSFO slips.

text.p: U.S. spot fuel oil prices, helped by firmer crude and gas futures, mostly held steady Tuesday in quiet trade, but high sulphur grades were pressured by soft demand and prospects for better avails, sources said.
"Without the (cold) weather, it's tenuous. We need some demand," said a cash trader, noting weaker bunkers and talk of rising Venezuelan supplies were pressuring high sulphurs.
In New York Harbor, high sulphurs eased, with 2.2 percent quoted slightly lower at $20.25-50 and three percent down a quarter at $19.50-75, traders said.
But with resid still the fuel of choice compared to gas, and winter still ahead, few expected fuel oil prices to collapse anytime soon.
NYH physical one percent was unchanged at $22.25-50, with December paper pegged higher early at $22.25-50 and January up 25 cents to the $22.65-90 range.

At the U.S. Gulf, one percent held steady at about $19.50, while three percent slipped 50-75 cents to $17.50-75 on softer bunkers in the region. Traders said a barge-size lot of 3.5 percent sold at $16.50 (delivered Houston).
New York city gate swing gas was talked down slightly in the $4.20s/mmBtu compared to NYH one percent resid at a $3.55/mmBtu equivalent.
